hints.title: Two Endpoints Choice
hints.text: At each operation step i, you either choose the leftmost available element or the rightmost available element.

hints.title: Derive Right Boundary from Left
hints.text: If left elements have been taken from the start, exactly i - left elements have been taken from the end, determining the right index.

hints.title: Two-Dimensional Dynamic Programming
hints.text: Define dp[i][left] as max score after i operations with left choices from front, taking the max of picking left or right.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumScore(self, nums: list[int], multipliers: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        m = len(multipliers)
        dp = [0] * (m + 1)

        for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            mult = multipliers[i]
            for left in range(i + 1):
                right = n - 1 - (i - left)
                pick_left = mult * nums[left] + dp[left + 1]
                pick_right = mult * nums[right] + dp[left]
                dp[left] = max(pick_left, pick_right)

        return dp[0]
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Branching left and right at each of m steps explores 2^m possibilities.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Memoizing states (i, left) reduces computation to O(m^2) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate deduces that right boundary is implicitly determined by n - 1 - (i - left).
